citations.quote: For an integer $n\ge2$, put $T_n=\mathbb R^2/(n\mathbb Z)^2$, with horizontal circles $\alpha_i=\{y=i\}$ and vertical circles $\beta_j=\{x=j\}$ for $i,j\in\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$. A **toroidal grid diagram of grid number $n$** is a pair of disjoint sets $\mathbb O,\mathbb X$ of points in the open cells of this grid such that every row and every column contains exactly one point of each set. At each crossing of the projected link, the vertical segment is over and the horizontal segment is under. Orient each horizontal segment from its $O$-marking to its $X$-marking and each vertical segment from its $X$-marking to its $O$-marking. The markings and these segments determine an oriented link. Following each component from an $O$ along its row to an $X$ and then along that column to the next $O$ defines a permutation of the $n$ $O$-markings; its cycles are the link components. The grid represents a knot precisely when this permutation is one $n$-cycle.

derivations.claim: In column $M$ the two markings lie at $H,K$. The interval $[H,K]$ lies strictly inside the interval $[D,T]$ of $B$, because $D<H<K<T$. Columns $B,M$ are adjacent. Their exchange is therefore an allowed nested-interval commutation, giving stage 1. It carries the whole column, including both exterior markings of $B$, and makes $L,M$ adjacent. No other mark changes its row.

Stabilize the marking $a$ at $(L,H)$, inserting $V$ immediately right of $L$ and $J$ immediately above $H$. Put $a$ at $(L,J)$ and $(V,H)$, put $\bar a$ at $(V,J)$, and leave $(L,H)$ empty. Thus the new block has northwest $a$, northeast $\bar a$, southeast $a$, and empty southwest: it is an $a:\mathrm{SW}$ stabilization. The former other marking $(M,H)$ of row $H$ stays on that row, and the former other marking of column $L$ stays in that column. Row $H$ now has $(V,a),(M,\bar a)$; row $J$ has $(L,a),(V,\bar a)$; all columns and rows still contain one of each type. Row $K$ remains $(M,a),(R,\bar a)$. This proves stage 2 with column order $L<V<M<B<R$ and row order $H<J<K$.

Rows $J,K$ are adjacent. Their closed horizontal intervals are $[L,V]$ and $[M,R]$. Since $L<V<M<R$, these are disjoint, including their endpoints. Their exchange is an allowed commutation. It gives stage 3, with row order $H<K<J$ and the same labeled marking pairs. This exchange uses no shared-endpoint interval rule.

At stage 3, columns $V,M$ are adjacent and rows $H,K$ are adjacent. In their block the northwest cell $(V,K)$ is empty; northeast $(M,K)$ and southwest $(V,H)$ have $a$; southeast $(M,H)$ has $\bar a$. The other marking of the two-row block is $\bar a$ at $(R,K)$, outside these two columns. The other marking of the two-column block is $\bar a$ at $(V,J)$, outside these two rows. This is an $a:\mathrm{NW}$ stabilization block in reverse. Contract it by deleting column $M$ and row $K$, retaining $a$ at the merged corner $(V,H)$, and moving the exterior block marking $(R,K)$ to $(R,H)$. The marking $(V,J)$ stays in column $V$. After renaming $V$ as $M$ and $J$ as $K$, the two rows are exactly $H:(M,a),(R,\bar a)$ and $K:(L,a),(M,\bar a)$. Each retains one $O$ and one $X$.

The stabilization inserted $V$ between the adjacent columns $L,M$; deletion of the old $M$ makes $V$ occupy precisely that old column's rank. Similarly $J$ was inserted between the adjacent rows $H,K$, exchanged with $K$, and remains at the original $K$ rank after the old row $K$ is deleted. Therefore the three-move subcertificate changes no other row or column rank and realizes exactly the exchange of the two original row contents. Column $L$'s lower partner and column $R$'s lower partner stay fixed, while the only exterior displacement in the complete four-move certificate is the already specified exchange of columns $B,M$ in step 1.1. All untouched rows and columns retain their marking counts. This verifies the full exterior marking assertion, not merely the unmarked local arcs.
